items.title: The tense line
items.caption: One sentence run across all four particles. Only the first word changes, and with it the time. Both pasts sit before now: what separates *sā* from *na* is the shape of the event, not how long ago it was.

points.label: sā
points.note: The past of how things were: states and habits that held over a stretch of time.

points.label: na
points.note: The past of a single, bounded event, a thing that happened once. The plain English "I went" fits both pasts.

points.label: ʻua
points.note: It does not send the event back in time. It marks a change, and reports that a new state is usually in place now.

points.label: ʻoleʻā
points.note: It places the event ahead of now: something expected to happen, usually quite soon. Its short form is *ʻā*.

items.title: The compass
items.caption: Five direction nouns carry the compass, two of them for the south. Tap one to read it.

points.label: sisifo
points.sm: ʻO le nuʻu i sisifo o le uafu.
points.en: The village west of the wharf.
points.note: One of the two direction nouns recorded in the frame, with the place it is reckoned from in the belonging slot.

points.label: saute
points.note: One of the two words for the south. The other is *toga*.

points.label: toga
points.note: The second word for the south, beside *saute*.
